issues.title: Keyspace-failure branch skips the immediate non-shard-aware fallback/retry
issues.verdictReason: The new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm at connection_pool.rs:900-911 ignores evt.requested_shard entirely and always sets had_error_since_last_refill, unlike the sibling Connection-error arm which retries immediately via start_opening_connection(None) without backoff when requested_shard.is_some(); since UseKeyspaceError includes transient variants (e.g. RequestTimeout, used in the new test), an immediate retry could plausibly succeed sooner than waiting for the backed-off refill.
issues.scopeReason: The Keyspace arm and its retry semantics are new code added by this PR.

issues.title: No bound or transient/permanent distinction on repeated USE (keyspace) failures
issues.verdictReason: When USE keeps failing (dropped keyspace, permission error, etc.), every new connection hits the Keyspace error arm, the pool stays empty and republishes Broken(UseKeyspaceError) each time with growing backoff via the existing reconnect policy; there's no special-casing of permanent vs transient keyspace errors. This mirrors how the codebase already treats other persistent connection errors (also unbounded, backoff-only), so it's a real but modest, consistent-with-existing-design limitation rather than a new class of bug.
issues.scopeReason: This retry/backoff behavior for keyspace failures did not exist before the PR (previously a failed USE never blocked or broke the pool at all).

reportedAsByRun.sonnet-5-5-2026-09-30/quillstone/ce-code: Nothing bounds this or distinguishes permanent from transient errors, and there's no test for repeated failures.
reportedAsByRun.sonnet-5-5-2026-09-30/quillstone/mattpoc: A transient failure (timeout, IO error) is reported the same as a permanent one (BadKeyspaceName, nonexistent keyspace), and the pool will keep reconnecting and failing USE indefinitely with growing, unbounded backoff.

issues.title: "Failed USE now marks node Broken instead of keeping the connection" framed as a…
issues.verdictReason: This is the PR's explicit, intended fix, not a regression: the PR body states 'A failed USE on a newly opened connection is now returned to the pool as a keyspace setup error. Before this PR, a connection that failed USE was silently added to the pool anyway despite having the wrong active keyspace, which is the actual bug being fixed; discarding it and surfacing Broken(UseKeyspaceError) when the pool empties is the correct, intended behavior change.

issues.title: Metric decrement/removal logic verified to avoid double-decrement
issues.verdictReason: Traced remove_connection (line 1216+): it only calls dec_total_connections when it actually finds and swap_removes the Arc from conns or excess_connections, and the connection_errors watcher (wait_for_error) checks Weak::upgrade() first, so once a connection is dropped via excess_connections.clear()/conns.clear() its error future silently no-ops instead of double-decrementing. full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics passes, empirically confirming no double counting.
